column1: # p381 — ACTION p379-A DISCHARGED.  THE RANDOM ARM OVER CHANNEL-B-ONLY ADDRESSES.
# p379 probed a DELIBERATELY ENRICHED sample: 24 of 49 live, published as an UPPER BOUND on the
# channel-B live rate and registered as needing a random arm to become a rate.  This is that arm.
# SAMPLING RULE, STATED BEFORE THE NUMBERS (Gap 540 is what its absence costs):
#   sample     = random.Random(381).sample(population, 40)     <- seed is the pass number, reproducible
#   probe      = git ls-remote https://github.com/<addr> HEAD   <- first-hand, serial, one per address
# RESULT: 26 LIVE of 40 = 65.0 %, against p379's enriched 24 of 49 = 49.0 %.
# 🔴 AND IT REFUTES THE FRAMING THAT REGISTERED IT.  p379 published its enriched figure as an
# UPPER bound.  The random arm is 16 POINTS HIGHER, so the enrichment selected for addresses that
# were MORE likely to be dead, not less.  The mechanism is in p379's own text: it reports that
# >= 73 of the channel-B-only addresses "sit beside a death or refusal marker ONLY".  An address
# this base DISCUSSES without linking is disproportionately an address a pass PROVED DEAD —
# so "enriched for discussion" is enrichment TOWARD the dead.  Direction, not magnitude, is the
# error, and no cell on this base records a sample's SELECTION RULE.  Gap 540.
# 🔴 SECOND FINDING, IN THE DENOMINATOR.  Two of the 40 are not repositories at all —
# `feature/openedx-integration` and `feat/cloud-rubric-tabs` are git BRANCH NAMES harvested as
# bare slugs.  Both probe DEAD, so the liveness arm absorbs them; the CENSUS does not.  p351's
# address-shape instrument passes both, correctly by its own contract, because `feature/x` is a
# legal owner/repo shape.  Among the 38 shape-plausible addresses the live rate is 26/38 = 68.4 %.
# BOTH figures are published because the denominator choice is the finding.  Gap 539.
